assessment_summary: The statement is false. Graphs that satisfy the premise (G-v is Hamiltonian for every vertex v) but do not satisfy the conclusion (G is Hamiltonian) are known as hypohamiltonian graphs. The smallest and most famous example of such a graph is the Petersen graph. The Petersen graph is a connected, simple graph on 10 vertices that is notoriously non-Hamiltonian. However, the removal of any single vertex leaves a graph on 9 vertices that contains a Hamiltonian cycle. Since the Petersen graph fulfills the hypothesis but violates the conclusion, it serves as a concrete counterexample, invalidating the statement.
counterexample: The Petersen graph is a counterexample. It is a connected, simple graph with 10 vertices. It does not contain a Hamiltonian cycle. However, deleting any vertex from the Petersen graph yields a subgraph on 9 vertices that does contain a Hamiltonian cycle (it is a hypohamiltonian graph). Therefore, it satisfies the condition that G-v is Hamiltonian for all v, but G itself is not.
